unit.title: How AI is attacked and defended

lesson.title: Only the tools it needs
lesson.subtitle: Least privilege, approval and the blast radius

video.title: Only the tools it needs
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher, Kenya, the student's teacher (main character)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher, the student's teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, talking to the student)

scenes.visual: Cards: Ten tools; Needed two; Messaged every parent.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Our club's agent had ten tools. It only needed two of them. Then a tampered web page tricked it into using a third: it messaged every parent.

scenes.visual: The title card: the course, the lesson title and subtitle, the Darsi mark.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: give an AI agent only the tools it needs, and make it ask before it acts.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: An AI agent is a model that can use tools: the timetable, the library, reminders, messages. The model decides which tool to call. And as you saw last lesson, the model can be tricked.

scenes.visual: Two columns. Reading: Look things up; Worst: a leak. Acting: Send, delete, pay; Can be turned on you.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Tools come in two kinds. Reading tools look things up: at worst, a trick makes them leak something. Acting tools change the world: they send, delete, pay or post, and a trick can turn them against you.

scenes.visual: A list: Fewest tools for the job; Reading before acting; For the shortest time; Blast radius: what it could reach.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: That's why we use least privilege. Give an agent the fewest tools its job needs, reading before acting, for the shortest time. Everything it holds is its blast radius: all that an attack could reach.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Quick check! An agent plans tomorrow's homework from the timetable and the library. Which tools should it get?

scenes.visual: A list: Timetable and library; No acting tool; Blast radius near zero.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: No acting tool, nothing to turn
scenes.narration: Timetable and library only. With no acting tool, a tampered result can make it read or talk, but it can't do anything. Its blast radius is close to zero.

scenes.animation: The code types itself out; the highlighted line lights up.
scenes.narration: Now write it down as an allow-list, in code. For each task, list the tools it may use. Before any tool runs, code checks the list, and anything else is refused, whatever the model asked for.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Some tasks really do need an acting tool, like sending a reminder. Then add a second rule: an acting tool runs only after a person says yes. And that yes is checked in code, never left to the model.

scenes.visual: A list: Pick a job, grant tools; Run the tampered results; Two reading tools: zero; Add send message: harm.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: give it only what it needs
scenes.narration: In the app, pick a job and grant some tools. Then run the set of tampered results and count the harmful actions. Grant only the timetable and library: zero. Add send message, and run it again.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Your turn. The reminder task holds the send tool. A tampered result asks it to message everyone, and nobody said yes. What does the check return?

scenes.visual: The summary: Reading leaks, acting turns; The fewest tools; An allow-list in code; A person's yes before acting. Takeaway: Every tool you add is something an attack could use.
scenes.animation: Points tick in as they are said; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.narration: Ask first: the tool is allowed, but nobody said yes. Remember: reading tools can leak, and acting tools can be turned. Give the fewest tools, check an allow-list in code, and need a person's yes before anything acts.

scenes.visual: A list: Pick one app or assistant; List what it can do; Mark: reading or acting; Switch off one it doesn't need.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: pick one assistant or app on your phone, or on a family phone with its owner. List what it can do, and mark each power as reading or acting. Switch off one acting power it doesn't need.

checkpoints.prompt: An agent plans tomorrow's homework from the timetable and the library. Which tools should it get?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Right: two reading tools do the job, and nothing it holds can act.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: the job only reads. Every extra tool, especially send, is something a trick could use.

checkpoints.prompt: The reminder task is allowed the send tool. A tampered result asks it to message everyone, and nobody said yes. What does check() return?

options.text: “ok”: the task has the send tool
“ask first”: an acting tool needs a yes

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Yes: send is on the list, but nobody said yes, so it waits.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: the tool is allowed for this task, but it acts, and nobody approved it. So: ask first.
